So because of the tiny population north of  delaware, there's not enough people for kaiser permanente , to operate up here. Even with new jersey, that's not enough potential customers , so they stop at brooklyn.

This\nIs how many Macy's department stores?I had to choose from near where I lived and worked, And that ain't even counting delaware. This is probably why i'm having difficulty finding other people who like board games or dungeons and dragons, I'm used to living in a area with A lot more people , so with only one in a thousand of us like something , that's still a sizable amount of people.

Diary

Session 1 – Prelude: A Few Grains of Sand
Dragon attack! Jane and Joseph fought a baby gencast dragon in an old ruin. They didn’t want to, but a voice was commanding the dragon, and the pair used their magic to defeat it.
The illusions of the ruin dissolved, revealing a metal room. A med team went to the dragon while Director Rodrick of the Dragon Warrior Academy applauded them (and the experimental dragon) on their test – they were now ready for missions for the Dragon Warriors.
As they were leaving, they bumped into a janitor clutching a mop and wearing a metal backpack, Avlae Pinooloo, who fangirled over the party and wanted to shadow them, though she expressed doubt that finding the True Dragons would be possible. Rodrick then asked the party to repair a laser turret that had become detached from the space station (called the Hourglass).
Unfortunately, all their dragons were sick, so they would have to do the job without them. The party got into space suits and cleverly used their magic to repair the turret. They also found possible signs of sabotage.
The party went to bed. Jane was awoken by something. Then a dragon landed on her window…and it broke the glass, and she was sucked into space! But her magic and Joe managed to bring her back inside, and they went to see what was happening.
Turned out: A full-on assault, with squadrons of dragons firing at the station and troops boarding. Rodrick tried to gain control of the situation while the party fought some invaders. Rodrick found the command room was out of commission, so the backup emergency button, in the bottom half of the Hourglass, would have to be reached in order to get reinforcements from the nearby planet LAX.
With Pinooloo tagging along, the party made a plan. They donned space suits and went outside the station, sneaking along its side with Joe's magic providing some propulsion, in order to sneak past the enemy. They managed to get to the lift separating the two halves of the Hourglass, but found it guarded. Jane used an invisible force to pull the dragon riders’ space suit tubes, distracting them and allowing the party to sneak inside to find the inside of the lift. They found it guarded, but much less than the outside, and took out the soldiers (Jane slitting the throats of the unconscious ones).
As they entered the lift, Pinooloo was suddenly shot! They dragged her into the lift and started the descent. Joe healed Pinooloo, but it didn't seem effective.
But as Jane and Joe prepared to exit the lift, they suddenly found Pinooloo tearing a hole in the wall with her mop-turned-halberd! She said sorry, but this was her operation and she wanted the party dead. She was a fan, but really, they were just like a couple grains of sand – what could they really accomplish? Her backpack unfolded into dark armor and she finished her hole, and she was sucked into space as a dragon filled the hole (Jane managing to get in a parting insult at Pinooloo).
Joe magic-shoved the dragon away, and, as the lift finished its journey, they pulled themselves out. They managed to find the backup emergency button room…but found the door being held shut.
It was Blu, a classmate they liked. She seemed scared, but the party suspected she might be a traitor. They managed to convince her to let them in, and they pressed the emergency button.
They waited…and waited…finally a dreadnought appeared, and the enemy was sent into retreat!
Rodrick congratulated the party, and told them that the next high-priority mission was definitely theirs. (Also, the party really wanted to talk to the Dragon Warriors Council about adding extra emergency buttons and background checks for janitors…)

Session 2 – Deep Secrets Part I: Gossip
Five days after the attack, Jane and Joseph went into the Dragon Warrior Council meeting, where the council was bickering about what to do about the attack. Though it was kind of hard to get the council to listen, the party did manage to suggest getting the Scalax Realm’s senate to communicate with the Scalax Realm’s allies about the Bloodfire Empire.
Also, the liquid found in the magic vial in space turned out to just be water. Jane hypothesized that it might have been used to freeze the turret's latches to make it easier to break them. The dragons being sick during the attack was also found to be the result of poison. Additionally, prisoners from the attack revealed that the Empire intended to take the station and kill several people, including, most likely, Jane and Joe.
The party, eager to get information, asked Rodrick to go investigate. He said that there might be a mission soon – a Warrior on the surface of LAX Prime may have found something – but they could probably take a few days off. So they got some dragons and went to Lith, a mostly neutral, self-contained system, on the edge of Bloodfire Empire territory. They sniffed around the system's teleportation circle space station and found someone who lost an uncle in a recent Bloodfire attack. Apparently, Bloodfire agents entered a neutral trading post space station, the Trim Barrel, in disguise, tried to buy a perhaps dragon-related piece of paper, and then chaos suddenly erupted and the station was blown up, leaving few survivors (though a significant number of the stations’ defensive dragons were “missing,” not “confirmed dead”). While there, the party also found out that the Dragon Warriors, being government agents, weren’t trusted by some elements of society, and the Dragon Warriors were considered particularly weird and nosy.
The party then went down to the surface of Lith Prime and entered one of the more civilized cities, hiding their identities as dragon warriors. While Joe stayed behind to guard the dragons and talk with local police – who have been on the lookout for potential Bloodfire agents – Jane went into town in hunt of rumors and information. She found a little carnival with a lot of people and found a shady-looking, whispering group. She overheard them talking about the city’s defenses. She then, intending to get a better look at them, went up to them, pretending to be asking about where to get a drink, and one of them put a pistol to her stomach.

Session 3 – Deep Secrets Part II: Seedy Alleyways
Jane managed to talk her way out of being immediately shot, but she was soon lured into an alley by the shady-looking group and ambushed. She called for backup and managed to hold off the attackers until Joe got there, dragons blazing. The party killed two and took the last, a cat person, hostage. Joe used charming magic to get the cat person talking, and they found that the Bloodfire Empire was infiltrating and investigating the defenses of cities around the planet in preparation for invasion. The party then handed the cat over to the local police and headed back to the Hourglass for their next mission.
An agent on LAX Prime, Boris, had found a tourist that had found a secret second layer to a ruin on the planet. They were to meet Boris in a bar beneath the city of Draco Minor so he could lead them to the ruin and investigate it for dragon lore. However, when they got there (after getting Jane some better armor), they found him missing. His cloak was at a booth, and he was last seen at a designated smoking area. There, Joe used magic to talk to the sea life outside the underwater tunnel and found that Boris had been kidnapped by three people with fire-shaped ice tattoos. So they went off in search of Boris…

Session 4 – Deep Secrets Part III: Coldtists
Jane and Joseph were stopped by someone whose cart apparently broke, but then they found themselves ambushed by two bounty hunters who were looking for them, as well as a third Dragon Warrior. Just then, Adrian, the third Dragon Warrior, arrived just as things were getting ugly, and though the two bounty hunters called in reinforcements – which ended up being a shooter in a building – the bounty hunters were defeated with the help of Adrian’s martial arts skills, with only the shooter surviving and getting away. Adrian, who’d been chasing down a lead for dragon lore that hadn’t panned out, decided to join Jane and Joe on their quest.
Joe talked to a squid and some dolphins for directions for where Boris had gone, then invited the animals to come with. The party found a building with scratches likely from a metal foot, and in the alley next to it they found a homeless-looking guy with an ice-fire tattoo pretend-sleeping in front of a door. Jane tried and failed to kill him via insults, then Joe intimidated him into getting his boss. Joe then turned into a mouse and followed him inside, finding Boris tied up in a room with a bunch of carousing gang members, called “the Coldtists.” He began nibbling on Boris’s ropes.
Meanwhile, the party’s squid friend was warning Jane and Adrian that people were coming. They tried to act natural, but the people coming were more coldtists, and they were suspicious of where the homeless guy was, and Adrian killed one of the guys and intimidated the other into bringing them inside. There, they found Boris, along with the leader of the Coldtists, Thingo. They managed to convince him that they had NOT killed one of his guys (whose name was Log) and wanted to negotiate for Boris’s release. Apparently, Boris had cost the Coldtists a shipment of laser guns, so Adrian offered him ten bags of 21 gold pieces each, giving him one of the bags as proof. Thingo accepted, and the party grabbed Boris (whose ropes came off real easy) and hustled out, just as Thingo shouted that they’d been swindled (the other nine bags were empty!). The party was chased by the Coldtists, but Joe used magic to break up the terrain behind them, and they got away.
They introduced themselves to Boris, and he told them that he had a key that would unlock an unexplored portion of a ruin. He left it with a friend, Lef (Lev? Lif? Left?), and they went to his place. But he wasn’t there, and he didn’t answer Boris’s watch call. The party went to a nearby pawn shop to see if Lef(?) had sold it, and, through Jane's truth magic and intimidation, the pawn shop owner revealed that Lef had sold it to him a couple hours ago, then someone had bought it half an hour later. That person had also bought an “I love beer” pin, so the party went in search of a bar…
